::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Computing the Path Integral of a Complex Function](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3627142/computing-the-path-integral-of-a-complex-function), asked by [guts](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/543210/guts) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-04-15; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> My question is given as:
>
>  $\gamma \ : \ [0,\pi] \rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ for the function $\gamma(t)=2e^{i6t}$, compute the path integral $\int_\gamma z^5 dz$
>
> My attempt so far is $$\begin{align}\int_\gamma z^5 dz & = \int_0^\pi \gamma(t)^5 \gamma'(t) dt \\ &= \int_0^\pi (2e^{i6t})^5 (12ie^{i6t})dt \\ & = 384i \int^\pi_0 e^{36it} dt \\ & = 384i \bigg[\frac{-1}{36}ie^{36it}\bigg]^\pi_0 \\ & = 384i \bigg(\frac{-1}{36}i--\frac{1}{36}i \bigg) \\ & = 0
> \end{align}$$
>
> I don't believe this is correct because I got 0, could anyone clarify if what I have done is correct?
>
> Help is greatly appreciated.
:::

According to [Cauchy's integral theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy%27s_integral_theorem), this is entirely expected.  It says that if $f \colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is holomorphic, and $\gamma$ is a simple closed curve, then $$\oint_\gamma f\,dz = 0$$.
